public_rationale: The March 2, 2026 repository says its verdicts are LLM-scored, not human-verified, and reflect evidence available as of March 2026 [e1]. That evidence cannot establish whether virtually every distinct AI warning Marcus gave over the preceding several years had come true by August 20, 2026 [e1].
limitations: The packet lacks a substantially complete, deduplicated inventory of warnings and independently verified outcomes through August 20, 2026.
The statement gives no precise starting date or numerical threshold for 'virtually every'; the surrounding examples concern surveillance.
The evidence does not establish which warnings were fulfilled under their original conditions and deadlines, contradicted, or still unresolved. Pending warnings are not automatically false.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Virtually every warning Marcus has given about AI over the last several years has come true.

statement.excerpt: Virtually every warning that I have given for the last several years has come true.
statement.document_title: OpenAI is becoming a surveillance company

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that almost all distinct AI warnings Marcus issued during the preceding several years had been borne out by August 20, 2026.
Repeated versions of one warning should not count as separate successes.
A warning counts as fulfilled only when its stated outcome and any conditions or deadline have been satisfied by the post date.
No exact starting year or percentage is supplied. The target period therefore retains an unspecified start rather than inventing one.
Warnings still awaiting their outcomes cannot be counted as already fulfilled, but are not automatically false.
criteria.support_condition: A substantially complete, reproducible inventory and independent outcome audit shows almost all distinct warnings fulfilled by the post date, with the conclusion robust to reasonable window and counting choices.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The same audit identifies a substantial share of warnings that had not come true by the post date, making an almost-all success claim untenable.
